# Images

The below HTML code displays the image below it.


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
![](/images/quarto_quarters.png){style="width:200px" fig-align="center"}
```
:::


<center>
![](/images/quarto_quarters.png){style="width:200px"}
</center>

You can customise the display with various parts.
Common inclusions for me are:


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
![](/images/quarto_quarters.png){style="width:200px; border-radius:5px; background:white; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}
```
:::


![](/images/quarto_quarters.png){style="width:200px; border-radius:5px; background:white; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}


The various options included above are:

- `style=`: Various style options
    - `width:`: sets maximum width of image 
        - Max width of our site's main are is 1000px, see [yml format](/yml/format.qmd)
        - Useful to do this way so images don't become tiny on a mobile phone.
        - If the width of the page is smaller than the set width it will interactively set the image to 100%
    - `border-radius:` adds curved corners, good for images with cornered background
        - 5px to 15px is generally a good range
    - `background:` sets the background colour
    - `border:` sets the colour style and thickness of a border
        - These three options can be in any order
- `fig-align=` sets the alignment of the image

Tips:

- You can use hexadecimals for colours (e.g. #111111)
- Ensure you have the `;` between the different options in `style=""`
